summary: Convert a decoded Yuv420Image to a packed sRGB Image for image operations, previews, and AI.
parameters: image: nullable Yuv420Image, such as value from spql.mcap.read_video

color_assumption: optional literal string or NULL. Accepted values: bt709_full, bt709_limited, srgb_bt709_full, srgb_bt709_limited, bt601_625_full, bt601_625_limited, bt601_525_full, bt601_525_limited.
returns: Nullable Image with contiguous RGB8 pixels, usable by spql.ai.score and Studio image previews.
details: Use spql.image.to_rgb(v.value) when range, matrix, primaries, and transfer are present. Inspect these fields directly from a bounded read_video query; omit the pixel planes. Prefer the recording configuration when it establishes missing metadata. When only primaries and/or transfer are missing, Studio permits a provisional profile for analysis that does not require calibration: for matrix bt470bg use bt601_625_*, for smpte170m use bt601_525_*, and for bt709 use bt709_*. Match the _full or _limited suffix to the observed range. This mapping is an analysis assumption, not recovered source metadata. Include color_assumption in the result and inspect representative converted frames to assess suitability for the task. Calibrated measurements require an established recording profile. If range/matrix are missing or no mapping applies, the provisional policy cannot supply a profile. H.264, pixel format, and resolution alone do not establish one. bt709_* supplies BT.709 matrix, primaries, and transfer; srgb_bt709_* supplies BT.709 matrix/primaries with sRGB transfer; bt601_625_* supplies BT.470BG matrix/primaries with BT.709 transfer; bt601_525_* supplies SMPTE 170M matrix, primaries, and transfer. Assumptions fill absent fields only and never override existing metadata; unsupported explicit metadata still fails. Omitted or NULL color_assumption requires complete metadata. Use only the accepted parameter values; planning may succeed before execution rejects an invalid value. This function converts decoded pixels; it does not decode video, repair packets, perform inference, or compute image metrics.

summary: Read the complete member population of an MCAP Dataset.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or spiral-dataset:<resource>:<version>:<data-revision> selector
returns: One row per member, including id (UUIDv7), source Blob, and bounded MCAP file statistics.
details: Use FROM spql.mcap.episodes('actual_dataset'). This is the cohort population, including members without the selected camera topic. Preserve these members when joining camera evidence. Inspect the relation schema before using file-statistic columns.

summary: Read one MCAP topic with its native message schema and member identity.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or exact spiral-dataset selector
topic: required literal string from the Dataset schema
variant: optional literal string; inspected schema fingerprint when the topic cannot unify losslessly
returns: id (UUIDv7), chunk_start_offset (UInt64), sample_ordinal (UInt32), log_time and publish_time (UInt64), sequence, channel_id, and value (schema-dependent message struct).
details: Use FROM spql.mcap.read_topic('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant'); arguments are literals, not per-row Blobs. foxglove.CompressedVideo value.data contains encoded packets and value.format identifies the codec. sample_ordinal is local to a chunk: it is not a stream-wide decode index, even if all its values happen to be unique. Zero does not prove a stream start or keyframe. Native message order within a member is determined by chunk_start_offset and sample_ordinal together. MCAP log_time is not automatically presentation time. For initial-frame, single-moment, or sparse-sampling tasks, assemble the native packet source with spql.video.from_packets, select frame references, then decode them. Use read_video only when the task needs the full video decoded.

summary: Decode a full foxglove.CompressedVideo H.264 MCAP video to YUV420 frames; use only when the task needs the full video decoded.
parameters: dataset: required literal string; Dataset name or exact spiral-dataset selector
topic: required literal string from the Dataset schema
variant: optional literal string; inspected schema fingerprint
returns: id (UUIDv7), log_time and publish_time (UInt64), chunk_start_offset (UInt64), sample_ordinal and frame_ordinal (UInt32), value (nullable Yuv420Image). Each row is a decoded frame.
details: Use only when the task needs the full video decoded. For initial-frame, single-moment, or sparse-sampling tasks, including pilot queries, use spql.video.from_packets with spql.video.frames or spql.video.frame_at, then spql.video.decode. Downstream filters and sampling do not avoid full-video decoding. Use FROM spql.mcap.read_video('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant'). Filter id and half-open log_time bounds to limit reads. The reader preserves packet order and decodes preceding parameter sets/keyframes and following GOP packets as support without emitting frames outside the requested bounds. Native log_time and publish_time remain attached to access units through decoder reordering; do not relabel them as inferred presentation time. Stable frame identity is id, chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal, frame_ordinal. sample_ordinal counts packets within a chunk. frame_ordinal is a zero-based index within each packet/access unit and resets for each packet. It is not a video-wide frame number: frame_ordinal < 1 selects the first frame of every packet, and frame_ordinal % 30 = 0 does not sample every thirtieth video frame. For a diagnostic read, select one episode, filter a short half-open log_time interval from observed timestamps, order by log_time, chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal, frame_ordinal, and LIMIT the output. LIMIT alone does not guarantee bounded decoding. For sampling across a video, establish temporal ordering within each episode and inspect the supported sampling/window functions; never use packet-local ordinals as global frame indexes. value is a decoded Yuv420Image with color metadata; do not call video.decode on it. Discover spql.image.to_rgb before passing it to Image-only operations or inspect_images. Raw Yuv420Image cells have no encoded image preview. Missing topics produce no frames. Unsupported codecs, missing random access, schema changes, and oversized GOPs fail explicitly. Validate and inspect a small bounded query before building a full-cohort analysis. Diagnostic SQL template (replace dataset, topic, variant, START_NS and END_NS with inspected values; choose a short interval for the selected episode): WITH e AS (SELECT id FROM actual_dataset ORDER BY id LIMIT 1) SELECT v.id, v.log_time, v.chunk_start_offset, v.sample_ordinal, v.frame_ordinal, v.value.range AS color_range, v.value.matrix AS color_matrix, v.value.primaries AS color_primaries, v.value.transfer AS color_transfer FROM spql.mcap.read_video('actual_dataset', 'actual_topic', 'actual_variant') v JOIN e ON v.id = e.id WHERE v.log_time >= START_NS AND v.log_time < END_NS ORDER BY v.log_time, v.chunk_start_offset, v.sample_ordinal, v.frame_ordinal LIMIT 3. This inspects metadata without inference. Once conversion succeeds, use the same bounds to select spql.image.to_rgb(v.value) AS image, with a documented assumption only if justified, and inspect those images before expanding the analysis.

summary: Expand encoded MP4 media into supported stream descriptions.
parameters: media: EncodedMedia
returns: One normalized stream-description row per supported MP4 stream.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.media.streams(input.media) stream. Inspect the output schema before selecting stream fields. No pixel decoding is performed.

summary: Expand an MP4 Blob into decode-order encoded sample rows.
parameters: blob: Blob
returns: Sample rows with container offsets, exact timing, sync status, and EncodedPacket values.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.mp4.read(input.blob) sample. This reads container samples without decoding pixels. Inspect the output schema before selecting sample fields.

summary: Expand an MP4 Blob into track headers.
parameters: blob: Blob
returns: One track-header row per supported MP4 track.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.mp4.tracks(input.blob) track. This does not decode samples. Inspect the output schema before selecting track fields.

summary: Read a Parquet relation with a schema resolved from its source.
parameters: path: required literal string
returns: Rows with the source Parquet schema.
details: Use FROM spql.parquet.read('actual_path'). The path must be available to the current project; do not invent a source path. Inspect the resolved schema before selecting columns.

summary: Generate integers in a half-open range.
parameters: overload 1: stop (Int64)
overload 2: start (Int64), stop (Int64)
returns: One value (Int64) per integer in [0, stop) or [start, stop).
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.range(input.start, input.stop) r for a range per input row. Null arguments or stop <= start produce no rows. The stop value is exclusive.

summary: Expand a video source and a native selection into frame references without decoding pixels.
parameters: source: StreamRef, EncodedMedia, or packet source from spql.video.from_packets
selection: FrameIndices, FrameSlice, or FrameTimes; FrameNeighborhood additionally supported for StreamRef and EncodedMedia, not packet sources
returns: request_index, requested_time, frame, time, duration. Selected frame references appear in request order, including duplicates.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.video.frames(input.source, input.selection) f, then spql.video.decode(f.frame) when pixels are needed. f is a relation alias, not a frame value. Discover the native frame-selection constructors and use their exact signatures. A packet source requires original decode order, in-band SPS/PPS, and an initial IDR; frame selection does not repair an incorrectly assembled stream. Do not assume the same fixed frame index exists in every episode.

summary: Describe one video stream from packet descriptors; requires original decode order and codec configuration.
parameters: packets: list of structs with payload (binary or Blob), decode_index (unique Int64), optional presentation_time (nanosecond duration)
codec: string; supported value h264
framing: string; supported value annex_b
returns: A packet-backed video source usable with spql.video.frames and spql.video.frame_at.
details: Construction is lazy. SQL assembles each stream with spql.list.collect(STRUCT_PACK(payload := payload, decode_index := decode_index)) grouped by episode/camera identity. Discover spql.list.collect as an aggregate; ARRAY_AGG and LIST are not its native names. In an earlier CTE, derive decode_index as CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY chunk_start_offset, sample_ordinal) - 1 AS BIGINT). The constructor sorts descriptors by decode_index, so aggregate ORDER BY is unnecessary. Frame indexing reads packet headers. Uniqueness alone does not establish correct order. Preserve each member/camera stream separately, in original decode order, including in-band SPS/PPS and an initial IDR. sample_ordinal from an MCAP reader is chunk-local and cannot alone supply decode_index. No MCAP schema or timestamp mapping is inferred. For initial-frame or sparse-sampling tasks, select frame references with video.frames or video.frame_at before video.decode. Use the source-aware MCAP video reader only when the task needs the full video decoded. An UndefinedPicParamSetId error can result from incorrect assembly; it does not establish that the source lacks parameter sets.

summary: Expand encoded media or a stream into presentation-order frame references without pixel decoding.
parameters: interval overload: source (StreamRef or EncodedMedia), optional start/end (nanosecond duration), optional fps (Float64), optional keyframes (boolean)
times overload: source (StreamRef or EncodedMedia), times (list of nanosecond durations), optional mode (string)
returns: frame, time, duration; times overload additionally returns request_index and requested_time in request order, including duplicates.
details: Use CROSS JOIN LATERAL spql.video.read(input.source, ...) f, then decode f.frame if pixels are needed. Omit optional arguments unless a supported value is known. Packet-backed sources use video.frames instead.

summary: Read a Vortex relation with a schema resolved from its source.
parameters: path: required literal string
returns: Rows with the source Vortex schema.
details: Use FROM spql.vortex.read('actual_path'). The path must be available to the current project; do not invent a source path. Inspect the resolved schema before selecting columns.
